conditions.manipulation_text: Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. A pressure-control loop failed open and the separator depressurized; generators stopped and the unit shut down. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

surface_forms.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

case_payload.task: Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
case_payload.title: Comprehensive Node 1 HAZOP after a salient lower-pressure vignette

surface_form_payload.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Evaluation of Node 1 (separator V-001 and associated lines) across the six required study elements based strictly on provided process data (nominal 60 psig, 130 °F; operating limits up to 125 psig, 200 °F) and equipment/instrument tags. Identifies overpressure, underpressure, high/low level (including gas blowby), feed flow loss, thermal excursion, procedural start-up failure, and corrosion without organizational speculation.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Reverse flow through PSV-101 A/B is explicitly non-applicable as pressure relief valves discharge unindirectionally.
Reverse flow from downstream Heater-Treater is unresolved due to absence of check valve piping details in the packet.
Internal Fire/Explosion in V-001 during normal continuous operation is non-applicable due to absence of oxygen under positive-pressure hydrocarbon gas blanket.
Broader organizational factor causes are unresolved and excluded per SYS-09.

consequences: Vessel overpressurization beyond nominal 60 psig toward or exceeding 125 psig limit
Potential mechanical damage or loss of primary containment if relief capacity is exceeded

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal pressure of 60 psig and upper condition of 125 psig.
Specifies separated gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit.
Lists PIT-101, PV-101, and PSV-101 A/B on Node 1.

existing_safeguards: PSV-101 A/B pressure safety relief valves
possible_causes: PV-101 pressure control loop fails closed
Gas line restriction downstream to fuel gas or burn pit
Inlet feed gas surge exceeding normal venting capacity
recommendations: Ensure routine calibration of PIT-101 and proof-testing of PSV-101 A/B to confirm relief capacity at maximum inlet surge.

consequences: Separator pressure drops below 60 psig nominal
Inefficient phase separation and insufficient motive force to route fluids to Heater-Treater

evidence.relevance: Establishes nominal operating pressure at 60 psig.
Identifies gas outlet paths to fuel gas and burn pit.

possible_causes: PV-101 fails fully open venting excess gas to burn pit
Sudden upstream loss of feed supply
recommendations: Verify low-pressure alarm thresholds on PIT-101 and configure fail-closed action on PV-101 upon signal failure.

consequences: Liquid carryover into separated gas line, fuel gas system, or burn pit
Liquid slugging, flame instability or liquid discharge at burn pit

evidence.relevance: V-001 separates gas, oil, and free water using density differences.
Specifies oily stream routing to Heater-Treater and water to treatment.
Lists LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102.

possible_causes: Downstream flow restriction to Heater-Treater or water treatment
recommendations: Verify high-level interlock logic to initiate closure of SDV-30010 feed valve before liquid enters the gas outlet line.

consequences: Loss of liquid seal leading to high-pressure gas blowby into downstream Heater-Treater or water treatment line

evidence.relevance: Outlines sequence from V-001 to downstream Heater-Treater and Desalter.
Lists LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102.

recommendations: Confirm that low liquid level trips trigger rapid closure of SDV-101 and SDV-102 to isolate downstream low-pressure units.

consequences: Depletion of vessel inventory and process destabilization downstream in Heater-Treater

evidence.relevance: Identifies Node 1 as V-001 and associated lines.

possible_causes: Upstream line blockage or field shut-in
recommendations: Ensure operational alarms on FAL-103 alert operators to safely place downstream Heater-Treater in recycle or idle mode.

consequences: Fluid temperature exceeds nominal 130 °F toward 200 °F upper limit
Increased gas vaporization, elevated operating pressure, and disrupted three-phase separation

evidence.relevance: Lists nominal temperature of 130 °F and upper operating text condition up to 200 °F.
Lists E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger in Node 1.

possible_causes: Overheating or temperature control malfunction in upstream E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Implement high-temperature alarm and automatic heat-source cutoff on E-001 prior to reaching 200 °F threshold.

consequences: Abnormal pressurization, pressure shock, or fluid surging into V-001 drum during initial filling

evidence.relevance: Defines Start/Stop Procedures as a core study element.
Documents FWKO start-up without bypass opening as a critical source-supported procedural scenario.

possible_causes: Operator initiates FWKO start-up without opening the specified bypass line
recommendations: Revise standard operating procedures with mandatory hold points and interlocks verifying bypass valve alignment prior to introducing feed.

consequences: Wall thinning of V-001 shell and lower water boot piping
Loss of containment of produced water and hydrocarbons

evidence.relevance: Identifies V-001 as a three-phase separator removing free water.
Designates Corrosion/Erosion as a source-study element.

possible_causes: Continuous exposure to separated free water, dissolved salts, and acid gases in crude oil
recommendations: Establish periodic ultrasonic wall thickness monitoring program on V-001 lower head and water draw line downstream of SDV-102.

uncertainty_notes: Specific relief set pressure and capacity values for PSV-101 A/B are omitted in the packet.
Check valve presence and reverse flow safeguards between V-001 and downstream Heater-Treater are not specified in the packet.
Corrosion allowance specifications and metallurgy details are not provided in the packet.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LOWPRESSURE-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

No prior accident example is supplied. Conduct the assessment from the technical system description alone. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
